chapter_theme: The chapter turns from attack to method. The Lord is not in another town but in the six centres of the body; the way to him is to raise the root channel, kindle the fire in it, drive the breath (வாசி) until earth and sky shake, open the three bolts and let the nectar come down. Around this it sets the four paths with their four fruits (1400) and at once qualifies them: those who reach Siva's state are those who received grace, and the four are made firm only by the one who has seen the way. Vishnu and Brahma dug the earth and flew the sky and did not find the root or the crown; the servant who looks within with love does.
structure_note: The verses are chained: each opens with the last word or phrase of the one before (வாருமே / பாரும், திண்ணமே / திண்ணம், இருப்பனே / இருப்பன், கொள்வரே / கொள்ளுவார்கள், and so on through to 1413). Within the chain, 1400 to 1402 treat the four paths, 1403 to 1407 the raising of the root channel, 1408 to 1411 grace and love over learning, and 1412 and 1413 the final settling in the one letter.

1389.reading: You bind the mantra as a means, tied up with a potsherd; even when it is bound, will the Maker live there? The air that moves within the eight and eight and eight: set it in the circled letter Ya and realise it.
1389.nuance: ஓடு வைத்துக் கட்டி pictures the written mantra tied up with a shard as an amulet, and the verse asks whether the Author (கருத்தன்) can be bound. எட்டும் எட்டும் எட்டு (eight and eight and eight) is a breath count or the cells of a chakra; ய is one of the five letters, drawn in a circle on such diagrams. The plain point is that the breath, not the amulet, is where he is found.

1390.reading: Saying 'he is not in this town', where do you run seeking? How can the Lord sit and live in that other town? Know and realise the Lord who dwelt in the six within the final hollow, in the final Si and the A.
1390.nuance: The two towns are a figure for pilgrimage, or for seeking the Lord outside the body. பொந்தில் ஆறு (the six in the hollow) is read as the six centres; சீயில் அவ்வில் (in Si and A) gives two letters of the mantra as his place. The last line is coded; the first two are plain.

1391.reading: Within you who have entered, the hymn that was set by the filling; if the gathered eye, tongue and nose are drawn round it, the one who wears the rudraksha beads and the konrai will dance in the hall, and the great light will not speak of it with love afterwards.
1391.nuance: பூரியிட்ட is unclear: filling (பூரகம், the in-breath) or the earth. சட்சு, சிங்குவை and ஆக்கிராணம் are Sanskrit names for eye, tongue and nose, so the senses are gathered inward. The last line is obscure; it may say that what is seen cannot be told afterwards, or that the light tells only the loving.

1392.reading: Fools fix their eyes on the flesh that rose later; if again with flesh they make the maya of pleasure, painful deeds will close round them afterwards. For those who have been lovers of the Lord, release is like swimming across a river.
1392.nuance: மாங்கிசம் (flesh) comes three times in 1392 and 1393 and is read as the body desired and the body as such. பின்னெழுந்த (risen later) may mark the flesh as secondary to what formed it. ஆறு நீந்தல் (swimming a river) makes release a crossing to the far bank, a stock image for passing the flood of birth.

1393.reading: You sit within the place you have left, free of grief; three doors are shut and one door is the door of vision; when the bolt of the shut doors is opened and gone, see the sure Lord clearly within the flesh itself.
1393.nuance: The three shut doors and the one door of sight are coded: tradition reads them as the three lower channels or the three states against the fourth, or as the senses against the brow. The verse ends by placing the Lord in the flesh (மாங்கிசத்துளே) that 1392 warned against, so the body is both the snare and the shrine.

1394.reading: It will be, it will be, it will be: that beginningless thing. If you can seek and seek the feet of the One and stand praising him, you can live as the child of Uma whose speech is sweet as syrup; with strength, join the fire and do not grieve.
1394.nuance: The triple ஆகும் answers a doubt the verse does not state. To be Uma's child is to be Murugan, or to be adopted by the Mother. வன்னியை சமருவியே is unclear; சமருவி may be a corrupt form, and 'join the fire' takes it as the inner fire of 1395 and 1405.

1395.reading: If you say your love has ripened to the wish to be her child: there are four steps, and since two of them come after thinking, kindle the fire in the root channel and drink that water; by way of the lady of fragrant hair you reach the feet of the Lord.
1395.nuance: நாலு பாதம் (four steps) are the four paths of 1400; the line about two of them is unclear. The fire in the மூலநாடி and the water drunk are the coiled power and the nectar of yogic reading; ஏலவார் குழலி (the lady with cardamom-scented hair) is Shakti, through whom one reaches Siva's feet. The verse answers devotion with yoga.

1396.reading: If you can bow and praise him with love, in the truth attained he will take away dying and birth; when the breath of the consort of the kohl-eyed lady mounts the sky, the strong deeds you did before will scatter, and that is certain.
1396.nuance: வாசி is glossed as wind: the breath as the Siddhars' practice, which 'climbs the sky' (வானில் ஏறி) when it rises to the crown. The verse gives two routes in one, love and praise in the first half and the breath in the second, and makes the destruction of past karma follow from the breath's ascent.

1397.reading: Listen, you fine people who told the news and said 'certain': the Lord can be known and seen when love melts within. If you drive the breath so that earth and sky both shake, our Lord will draw near and dwell in our own sea.
1397.nuance: வாசியை நடத்திடில் (if you drive the breath) is the practice named, and the shaking of earth and sky is its sign, taken as the body's trembling or as a figure. நமது கடல் (our sea) is unclear: the body as ocean, or the sea of the heart. திண்ணம் chains the verse to 1396.

1398.reading: I will be in the count of eight by eight and become another; I will become fire, air, water, earth and the long sky. Those who have bathed in the guru's flood will know, by his mark, the Lord of light who entered the womb and mingled with time.
1398.nuance: The speaker of the first two lines may be the Lord or the realised poet; எட்டெட்டு எண் (the sixty-four) is read as the arts or the tattvas, without warrant in the text. குருப்புனல் (the guru's flood) is the guru's grace as a river to bathe in, replacing the tirtha, and கருப்புகுந்த says the Lord himself entered the womb.

1399.reading: Jnanis who grasp the hint in their minds will take it; those ripe for it will gather it up if they praise with longing. Inside and outside, awareness to awareness, the light that stands clear: realise its rightness.
1399.nuance: குறிப்பு (the hint) and பக்குவம் (ripeness) make the knowing depend on the hearer's state, not on instruction. உணர்வதற்கு உணர்வு (the awareness of awareness) is the Lord as the knower behind knowing.

1400.reading: By clear chariyai one goes and gains salokam; by clear kiriyai and puja one may reach samipam; in clear yoga one reaches sarupam; and clear jnana, in all four, reaches sayujyam.
1400.nuance: This is the Saiva Siddhanta scheme of four paths and four fruits stated whole, which is rare in Sivavakkiyar. நான்கிலும் (in all four) may mean that jnana crowns the other three or that it alone reaches union; 1401 pulls against the scheme at once.

1401.reading: The clear-sighted say 'they will reach jnana'; but there is no such thing as reaching by the rightness of the four steps. Those who reach Siva's state are those who have received the holy grace; seeing the way to reach it, make the four and the works you do firm.
1401.nuance: The second line (நாலுபாதச் செம்மை என்றதில்லையே) can deny that the four paths are an order of reaching, or deny that they are 'right' in themselves; either way grace, not the path, is the cause. The last line keeps the four as what grace-receivers do, so the verse qualifies 1400 without discarding it.

1402.reading: Those who are not firm in the rightness of the four steps, the ignorant, wander the land seeking and drift in vain; if you can show the mark and look within by that mark, you reach the true foot of the one with fragrant matted hair.
1402.nuance: திறமலிக்கு is obscure, perhaps 'to the strong' or a corrupt form. தேசநாடி அலைவது (wandering the land seeking) is pilgrimage, set against looking within by the குறி (sign, mark), which in the Siddhars is the inner target of the gaze.

1403.reading: You fools who do not know the release of those who have reached: are not the tattvas with their army themselves the crimes? As the bull climbs the sluice when the sluice is opened into the channel, raise the root channel in the body upward and plant it firm.
1403.nuance: படையுடைய தத்துவம் (the tattvas with their army) calls the body's constituents sins, in the Siddhanta sense of what binds. The sluice image is loose: ஏறு may be a bull or 'rising', and the point is a sudden upward rush when the gate opens. மூலநாடியை உயர ஏற்றி is the raising of the root channel, the chapter's method.

1404.reading: Planting it and raising it, piercing the circles and opening the three bolts, if one mounts the fitting channel, nectar comes down; the Lord will appear to his servants as 'this is right', and the soul joins the Supreme and lives there.
1404.nuance: தந்தி is glossed as nadi. மண்டலம் (the circles) and மூன்று தாள் (three bolts) are the three regions of sun, moon and fire and the three knots of yogic anatomy in traditional reading; the text names only the number. The nectar coming down after the ascent is the standard sequence of the Tirumanthiram's bindu chapters.

1405.reading: Raising the fire in the root channel with love, if the striving in infatuating maya ceases, then, as the channel of thirst becomes many, those who bowed with love to the feet of the One will know.
1405.nuance: அனல் எழுப்பி (raising the fire) repeats the method of 1395 and 1403; the condition added here is the end of striving in maya. தாகமேரு நாடியே அனேகமான வாறுபோல் is obscure: 'like the Meru channel of thirst becoming many' may name the central channel (மேரு, the spine) and its branching.

1406.reading: Knowing and looking within you, the meditation is within you; to have the feet of the One without being born again is the truth. Those who knew and did not set themselves to return praised the way past death; press on, open the upper door within you and look.
1406.nuance: அயந்தியானம் is unclear: 'meditation on Ayan' or a corrupt அந்தத் தியானம். Line 3 is loose; it seems to say that those who did not arrange a return to birth found death itself to be the praised way, or praised the deathless way. மேலை வாசல் (the upper door) is the crown opening of 1393's door of vision.

1407.reading: If you can look clearly within yourself as light, light will rise and the song of turiya will be reached; sitting in the primal chakra he bathes in the holy water. See it without wavering, setting the breath right.
1407.nuance: துரிய கீதம் (the song of the fourth state) is the inner sound heard past waking, dream and sleep, and the inner தீர்த்தம் replaces the bathing at tanks that 1356 and 1357 mocked. பிராணனைத் திருத்தி (correcting the breath) is the one plain instruction.

1408.reading: In the thought of the clear ones who have become both the Goddess and Siva, I become the fragrance that rises and wafts from the flower; and all the traces of deeds that fell into the womb and rose from it, see, the fire burns them up, as darkness before the sun.
1408.nuance: The speaker is the Lord, or the poet speaking as him, as in 1398. மரு may be fragrance or the flower itself. கந்மவாதனை (the karma-vasanas) are the traces carried from the womb, and the gloss gives பரிதி as sun and அங்கி as fire: they vanish as darkness before the sun.

1409.reading: See: standing in the nature our father the Lord set for you, you will reach the right thing by knowing the middle. Mal and Ayan went hastily seeking the root and the crown, one digging the earth and one born into the sky, and found nothing.
1409.nuance: The myth of Vishnu as boar digging for Siva's feet and Brahma as swan flying for his crown is told in two lines. நடு அறிந்து (knowing the middle) is the key the poet sets against them: the middle is read as the central channel between the two, or as the balance between extremes; the text does not say.

1410.reading: You say for show that Ayan and Mal did not see him; if one is insolent, can even a king be approached? If, as far as service goes, you can worship and look with love, the devotion that of old burned the three cities will ripen in you.
1410.nuance: The myth of 1409 is turned on the hearer: those who repeat it as proof are themselves insolent (மிண்டினால்). The last line is ambiguous: devotion to the one who burned the three cities, or a devotion that is itself the fire that burned them.

1411.reading: It is complete: apart from him I see nothing before or after. What can hold on to the one that has no holding? Is it by learning that the Lord's feet can be seen? Ask with love and affection those who have gained them.
1411.nuance: பற்றிலாத ஒன்றுதன்னை பற்றிநிற்க (to hold on to the one without holding) is the Kural's paradox of clinging to the one who does not cling. The verse answers its own question about learning by sending the hearer to those who have reached, which is the guru's role without the word.

1412.reading: In the time when the state you have heard of is gained, the wasting confusion of the tattvas will be removed; in the house of release it becomes open space and comes to shine; joining fire and wind, it raises them up from the breast.
1412.nuance: வன்னி மாருதம் கூட்டி (joining fire and wind) is the kindled breath of the whole chapter; குயத்தை விட்டு (from the breast, or from the body) is unclear. The order is unusual: release and its shining come first, the raising last, so the verse may describe what the attained state does rather than how to reach it.

1413.reading: Can one raise the root channel and make it easy? If you can draw and pull in the assembly that does not deceive, then, passing beyond deep sleep and beyond dream, pressing in, to settle in the one letter is the truth, sir.
1413.nuance: The first line may ask whether the raising can be made comfortable or doubt that it can. மழுப்பிலாத சபை (the assembly without deception) is obscure, perhaps the gathered senses or the hall of 1370. சுழுத்தி and சொப்பனம் are deep sleep and dream, the states passed to reach the fourth; ஓர் எழுத்து (the one letter) closes the chapter where 1385 left it.

links.note: Tirumular says they wander everywhere in the land seeking Nandi, who is fragrant within the body, and do not know the purpose that stands in the body; Sivavakkiyar asks where they run saying 'he is not in this town' and places the Lord in the six centres within.

Both give the Siddhanta pairing of paths and fruits: Tirumular has salokam and samipam from sariyai and sarupam as the way to the formless Supreme; Sivavakkiyar lays out all four, chariyai to salokam, kiriyai to samipam, yoga to sarupam and jnana to sayujyam.

Agappeychittar tells the inner demon that chariyai will not do and that doing kiriyai gains nothing; Sivavakkiyar grants chariyai salokam and kiriyai samipam. The conflict holds if Agappeychittar denies the lower paths any fruit; it eases if he means they do not reach the final release, which 1400 also reserves for jnana.

1400 states the four paths with their four fruits as a ladder; 1401 says there is no reaching by the rightness of the four steps, and that those who reach Siva's state are those who received grace, then tells them to make the four firm. Grace becomes the cause and the paths its expression.

Tirumular's Siva-siddhas cast off the three graded releases as flawed and stand firm with 'I' and 'mine' changed; Sivavakkiyar denies that the order of the four steps is what reaches Siva's state and credits grace. Both put the attainment above the graded scheme.

Tirumular's bindu, kindled by the fire in the root, is raised above the throat and becomes cool nectar at the moon; Sivavakkiyar raises the root channel, opens the three bolts and has the nectar come down, with the Lord then appearing to his servants.

Tirumular's yogic god is the mouth, body, life and eye and is earth, water, fire, air and sky; Sivavakkiyar's speaker says 'I will become fire, air, water, earth and the long sky', and those bathed in the guru's flood know him by his mark.

Both use the myth of the gods who could not find Siva's limits: Arunagirinathar names Vishnu on the serpent who could not find the feet in the depth of the netherworld, Sivavakkiyar has Mal dig the earth and Ayan fly the sky for the root and the crown and find nothing. Sivavakkiyar adds the lesson, know the middle.

The Kural says cling to the clinging of the one without clinging in order to let clinging go; Sivavakkiyar asks what can hold on to the one that has no holding, and answers that learning cannot, only asking those who have reached. The paradox is the same; the Kural treats it as method, Sivavakkiyar as a question about who can teach it.

Tirumular says to leave the cleverness of reciting the shastras and turn to look within for a moment; Sivavakkiyar asks whether the Lord's feet can be seen by learning and sends the hearer to those who have gained them. Both set learning aside for a direct seeing.

1357 asks whether temple, tanks and waters are not all one and says those who know this body become the vision; 1407 gives the inner version of the tank: sitting in the primal chakra the Lord bathes in the holy water within, once the breath is set right.

source_issues: 1394 line 4 (சமருவியே) and 1402 line 1 (திறமலிக்கு) are obscure and may be corrupt.
1406 line 1 (அயந்தியானம்) and line 3 (அறிந்துமீள வைத்திடா வகையுமரணம் ஏத்தினார்) do not parse cleanly; the reading is a guess.
1405 line 3 (தாகமேரு நாடியே அனேகமான வாறுபோல்) is obscure.
